claim_text: A third party copied payment card data stored on Cleverbridge's platform
summary: Cleverbridge's own incident page says it detected unauthorised activity in its platform on Nov 4, 2026, and that its investigation later determined a third party copied payment card data stored on the platform.
detail: BleepingComputer reports the same from the same page. The company calls the investigation ongoing. It does not say how the third party got in.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: The company's own page (Tier 1) states the copying; BleepingComputer read the same page and a customer notice.

claim_text: Cleverbridge detected the activity on Nov 4, took systems offline briefly and had them back the same day
summary: The company page says it detected unauthorised activity on Nov 4, 2026, took steps to contain it, temporarily took affected systems offline, and brought all systems back online on Nov 4.
detail: The page does not say when the third party first got in, how long they were there, or when the card data was copied. Systems being back on Nov 4 does not by itself show the intrusion lasted one day.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: The company page gives the dates; BleepingComputer repeats them.

claim_text: Cleverbridge began notifying affected people on Nov 20, with an outside notification firm
summary: The company page says it began notifying affected individuals on Nov 20 'where appropriate'. It says a TransUnion/Cyberscout service is sending the notices and offers affected cardholders credit or identity monitoring where available.
detail: BleepingComputer says notices began Nov 20 and names the same vendor. The company says its investigation continues and does not say how many people were notified.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: Stated on the company page and repeated by BleepingComputer.

claim_text: Card number, expiry date and CVV/CVC security code were taken, per a customer notice
summary: BleepingComputer was shown a breach notification that says the information involved includes the card number, expiry date and card security code (CVV/CVC), and that no other personal data such as name, contact or billing details was copied.
detail: The company's public page is less specific: it says the information 'may include payment card details' and refers people to their own notification. We have not seen a company statement on the exact fields, so this stays Reported. The company did not answer BleepingComputer's questions on whether the data was encrypted or why security codes were held.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: One outlet quotes a customer notice; the company page confirms only 'payment card details'.

claim_text: Cleverbridge says it was not a ransomware attack
summary: The company page answers 'Was this a ransomware attack?' with 'No. None of our systems were encrypted.'
detail: BleepingComputer repeats it. 'Not ransomware' says nothing about whether data was taken: the company confirms it was.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: The company's own FAQ states it; BleepingComputer repeats it.

claim_text: Cleverbridge's customers include Red Hat, SUSE, Tenable, Veeam, Jamf, Sony and Parallels, per BleepingComputer
summary: BleepingComputer lists these brands as Cleverbridge customers and says the company has not said which businesses' customers were affected.
detail: Cleverbridge's own site shows Red Hat, SUSE and Parallels among its client stories. Being a customer does not mean that business's buyers were affected. The page says affected people are those who bought from businesses Cleverbridge supports.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: BleepingComputer names the brands from the company's customer list; the company has not said which are affected.

claim_text: Malwarebytes says a small subset of its customers were affected
summary: A reply from the Malwarebytes support forum's admin account says Cleverbridge is a merchant-of-record payment processor it uses, that this was a breach of Cleverbridge's systems, and that only a small subset of its customers were affected.
detail: This is a forum post, so it is Tier 4. It names one seller whose customers were affected; it is the only affected business we found. It also says the company contacted affected customers.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: A forum post from the vendor's own admin account; no press or company statement confirms it.

claim_text: Cleverbridge told data protection authorities, law enforcement and card networks, per BleepingComputer
summary: BleepingComputer reports the company says it has notified data protection authorities, law enforcement, payment card networks and payment partners.
detail: We did not find this line on the company page we read.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: One outlet reports the company's statement; the company page does not repeat it.

claim_text: How many people and which businesses' customers were affected
summary: No count of affected cards or people, and no list of affected businesses, has been published.
detail: BleepingComputer asked the company about the number affected and received no reply by publication.
label: Not established
why_it_supports: Neither the company page nor BleepingComputer gives a figure.

claim_text: How the third party got in
summary: Cleverbridge has not said how the third party got into its platform or how long they were there.
detail: The page says only that the investigation is ongoing. No technical write-up has been found.
label: Not established
why_it_supports: Neither source gives a method or duration.

claim_text: Who is behind the Cleverbridge breach
summary: No attacker or claim of responsibility has been named by the company or the outlets we read.
detail: We did not look at leak sites or forums for claims, and would cite such claims only through press.
label: Not established
